content.readme:
# DeepInfer

DeepInfer is the high-performance inference framework that powers DeepSeek's large-scale production services. This open-source release provides offline inference with the core features needed for serving at scale.

Supported models:

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Supported features:

- Optimized kernels, model and sampler runtime
- Parallelism: Attention DP / balanced CP, MoE EP + EPLB
- DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification
- SWA bounded replay
- Asynchronous scheduling (zero-overhead batch scheduler)
- Batch-invariant inference
- Deterministic sampling
- Structured outputs

<details>
<summary>Feature details and configuration</summary>

- **Optimized kernels:** [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA), [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM), [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP), [TileKernels](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/TileKernels), [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect), and custom [TileLang kernels](deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops).
- **DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification:** accelerate decoding with draft tokens and use confidence estimates to schedule verification. Set `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`; `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE` controls the maximum draft length (default: 5).
- **Decoder SWA bounded replay:** reduce decoder prefill work by replaying only a bounded suffix. Set `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140` for the default V4.1 settings; the retained suffix must cover the SWA window plus the maximum backtracking length.
- **Asynchronous scheduling:** overlap CPU batch scheduling with device execution. Enabled by default.
- **Batch-invariant inference:** keep model results identical across different batch compositions. Enable with `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (NVIDIA only).
- **Deterministic sampling:** produce identical outputs for identical input tokens and sampling parameters. Set `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0` and pass a fixed `seq_seed` to `SamplingParams` (NVIDIA only).
- **Structured outputs:** constrain generation to a regex, JSON schema, or EBNF grammar. Pass `so_args={"schema_type": ..., "schema": ...}` to `SamplingParams`; see [examples](examples/_structured_output.py).

</details>

Supported hardware:

- NVIDIA SM100 GPUs
- Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

- A KV cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation (most required engine functionality is already implemented)
- Load balancing across data-parallel replicas for both prefill and decode

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Linux
- GCC >= 13.0
- Python 3.12
- CUDA 13 (NVIDIA only)
- CANN 9.2 (Ascend only)

### Build from source

Before building DeepInfer, please create and activate an empty Python 3.12 environment.

``` bash
# Use `ascend` instead for the Ascend platform
# Keep it exported in the environment where you run DeepInfer
export DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=nvidia
./build.sh
```

### Offline inference

The default checkpoint, [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017), is
downloaded into the Hugging Face cache on the first run; set `DEEPINFER_HF_MODEL_DIR=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` to
run from a local copy instead.

``` bash
python examples/offline_inference.py
```

See [examples](examples/README.md) for details.

## Performance benchmarks

| Prefill | Decode |
| :---: | :---: |
| [![Prefill: non-cached input throughput vs. latency](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png)](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png) | [![Decode: output throughput vs. per-user speed](doc/images/decode_pareto.png)](doc/images/decode_pareto.png) |

Measured on 4 SM100 GPUs for prefill and 64 for decode — each within one scale-up domain. To reproduce the benchmarks, see [run_sweep.sh](examples/sweep/run_sweep.sh).

## Evaluation benchmarks

See [eval/README.md](eval/README.md).

## License

DeepInfer is released under the Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

## Acknowledgments

DeepInfer was originally built primarily on [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), with additional inspiration from [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) and [TensorRT-LLM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM). We thank their developers.

## Citation

```bibtex
@misc{deepinfer2026,
  title = {DeepInfer: High-performance, large-scale inference framework for DeepSeek models},
  author = {DeepSeek-AI},
  year = {2026},
  publisher = {GitHub},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer}},
}
```

# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

content.readme:
![gpu-unlock: full-speed tensor cores for GeForce RTX](assets/banner.svg)

### Your GeForce runs AI at half speed. This fixes it.

![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.0-76b900)![RTX 20 | 30 | 40](https://img.shields.io/badge/GeForce-RTX%2020%20%7C%2030%20%7C%2040-76b900?logo=nvidia&logoColor=white)![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Linux-informational?logo=linux&logoColor=white)![License GPL-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--2.0-blue)![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Zagitta/gpu-unlock?style=flat&color=yellow)

**Up to 2× FP16 / BF16 / TF32 tensor throughput** · **+25–55% LLM prefill** · **+25–50% fine-tuning** · **+30–55% image generation**

[Supported GPUs](#supported-gpus) · [Benchmarks](#what-you-get) · [Install](#how-to-install) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Support](#support-me)

---

NVIDIA ships GeForce cards with their tensor cores capped to **half speed** for
FP16, BF16 and TF32 math with FP32 accumulation, which is what nearly all AI
training and unquantized inference uses. The same silicon sold as an RTX A-series
or professional card runs at full rate. `gpu_unlock` removes that cap at boot,
before the stock NVIDIA driver loads. No patched driver, no VBIOS flash, nothing
to redo when NVIDIA releases a new driver.

---

## Supported GPUs

| Generation                | Cards                                                                                                                  | Status                    |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **Ampere** (RTX 30)       | RTX 3050, 3060, 3060 Ti, 3070, 3070 Ti, 3080, 3080 Ti, 3090, 3090 Ti, plus RTX 3070/3080 Laptop GPUs                   | Stable, 100+ user reports |
| **Ada Lovelace** (RTX 40) | RTX 4060, 4060 Ti, 4070, 4070 SUPER, 4070 Ti, 4070 Ti SUPER, 4080, 4080 SUPER, 4090, 4090 D, RTX 4050/4060 Laptop GPUs | Experimental              |
| **Turing** (RTX 20)       | RTX 2060, 2060 SUPER, 2070, 2070 SUPER, 2080, 2080 SUPER, 2080 Ti, Titan RTX                                           | Experimental              |
| Blackwell (RTX 50)        |                                                                                                                        | Not supported             |

Laptops only stay unlocked if the dedicated GPU is never fully powered off.  
Many laptops power it down when idle, which silently resets the unlock. Turning  
off runtime power management with `options nvidia NVreg_DynamicPowerManagement=0x00`
in `/etc/modprobe.d/` helps on some models, but expect mixed results.

The exact PCI device IDs are in [`kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c`](kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c).
Linux only. For Windows see the [FAQ](#faq).

---

## What you get

The tensor core rate doubles. How much of that you see depends on how much of
your workload is FP16/BF16/TF32 matrix math, and on whether the card has the
power headroom to run it.

Dense matrix multiply (FP32 accumulation, stock power limits):

| Card | BF16 before | BF16 after | Gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 3060 12 GB | 27 TFLOPS | 51 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 3060 Ti | 37 TFLOPS | 68 TFLOPS | +82% |
| RTX 3070 | 40 TFLOPS | 72 TFLOPS | +81% |
| RTX 3080 10 GB | 65 TFLOPS | 113 TFLOPS | +73% |
| RTX 3090 | 75 TFLOPS | 125 TFLOPS | +65% |
| RTX 3090 Ti (450 W) | 88 TFLOPS | 157 TFLOPS | +80% |
| RTX 4070 Ti | 81 TFLOPS | 150 TFLOPS | +84% |
| RTX 4080 | 104 TFLOPS | 193 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 4090 | 165 TFLOPS | 329 TFLOPS | +100% (peak MMA rate) |

The RTX 4090 runs out of power before it runs out of tensor cores, so large
GEMMs at stock power limits gain much less than the peak rate suggests.

Real workloads:

| Workload | Typical speedup |
| --- | --- |
| LLM prefill / prompt processing, FP16/BF16 or AWQ/GPTQ (vLLM, PyTorch, Transformers) | +25–55% |
| Time to first token | 25–30% lower |
| LoRA and full fine-tuning in BF16 | +25–50% |
| Image generation, FP16/BF16 (SDXL, SD 1.5, Krea, DiT models in ComfyUI) | +30–55% |
| Video generation, BF16 compute (Wan 2.2) | +15–20% |
| FlashAttention / SDPA kernels | +50–60% |
| llama.cpp / Ollama with quantized GGUF | 0–15%, mostly at long context |
| LLM decode / token generation (memory bound) | No change |
| INT8, FP8 and INT4 models | No change |
| Gaming and FP32 CUDA | No change |

Outputs are bit-identical before and after; only the speed changes. These
numbers come from the [compatibility reports](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues)
users have filed, where you can find full benchmark details and post your own.

---

## How to install

First run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
cd gpu-unlock
make install
```

Then append `gpu_unlock.targets=all` to your kernel command line, keeping

content.readme:
# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

For Google Antigravity, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.agents/skills/` inside that project instead.

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

content.readme:
An agent harness for learning.

Download · How it works · Documentation · Issues · Discord

LearnHarness uses AI agents to plan and teach lessons from your current understanding to your goal. It builds a detailed picture of what you understand and how you reason. That picture is updated as you learn. Instead of just giving you an explanation, it uses your answers and thinking to decide what you need next. Teaching builds understanding one reasoning step at a time. Practice makes it usable. A persistent knowledge graph carries it across sessions. ![LearnHarness teaching session](docs/assets/teaching-session.png) ## How it works 1. **Measure.** Before teaching, the agent finds where your understanding ends on each part the lesson depends on. Your answers, confidence, and thinking show it where to start. 2. **Plan.** It works out a dependency map from that starting point to your goal. You can see the plan, and the lesson adapts when your understanding turns out different. 3. **Teach.** Each step builds on something you already understand. You predict, get an explanation, and check your understanding. Confusions are repaired before anything is built on them. The aim is for the goal to feel obviously true, not merely familiar. 4. **Practice.** Separate sessions pose varied problems that require the right knowledge to come to mind without being named first. Problems and hints adapt to your reasoning. **Think out loud.** The thinking fields let you explain your reasoning, uncertainties, and reactions in your own words. This is how the agent gets a detailed picture rather than just a record of right and wrong answers. You can type or use dictation. **Bring your files.** In the desktop app, attach PDFs, photos, or any other file with the paperclip, or drag them in. The file stays where it is: the message carries its path, and the agent reads it from there. The agent can also research questions in the background, create visual explanations, show your own images in the lesson and mark them up with arrows and labels, and build interactive demonstrations. ## Knowledge that carries forward What you are taught accumulates as propositions and reasoning chains: individual claims and the premises that lead to them. The graph shows this structure, with links back to the source sessions. You can also import notes. Future teaching sessions can read the graph instead of starting from scratch. Practice sessions can draw their material from it. It stores the ideas and their connections, not ratings of your ability. ![LearnHarness knowledge graph](docs/assets/knowledge-graph.png) ## Download and get started **[Download from learnharness.ai](https://learnharness.ai)** · [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/amosblomqvist/learnharness/releases) - **macOS (Apple Silicon):** signed and notarized DMG. Drag the app to Applications. - **Windows (x64):** run the installer. It is currently unsigned; Windows may show an “unknown publisher” or SmartScreen warning. - **Linux (x64):** make the AppImage executable and open it, or install the Debian/Ubuntu `.deb`. Choose your models, then start a session with what you want to understand. You can use provider API keys, supported subscription connections in the desktop app, an installed [Claude Code CLI](docs/claude-code.md), or a [custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint](docs/custom-providers.md), including a local model server. Optional dictation and web search use separate service keys. Web research can use a Tavily, Brave, Exa, Firecrawl, or Ollama key in Settings → Providers → Search. Ollama search uses its hosted service, not a local model server. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) for model setup, dictation, files, and notes imports, and [context, caching, and costs](docs/compaction-accounting.md) for advanced cache preferences. All three platforms support in-app updates. ## Your keys, your data - **Your keys and models.** No LearnHarness subscription or markup. The live cost meter estimates known API costs, not subscription, CLI, or custom-endpoint charges. - **Local storage.** Your chats, graph, settings, and API keys live on your machine. # Lichii Lichii is an experimental, open-source Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 emulator written in C++. It builds on Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, preserving their contributions while developing this fork's game compatibility and renderer fixes. This is an independent fork, not an official release of those upstream projects. Lichii is not affiliated with Nintendo. Visit the [Lichii game compatibility website](https://lichii.zortos.me) to find games and compare community compatibility reports. ## Downloads and setup Download Lichii only from this repository's [releases page](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases). Lichii has no other download site: archives offered elsewhere, such as lichii.org, are not built by this project, and one has been reported to install malware ([#545](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/issues/545)). On Windows, extract the entire build archive and run **lichii.exe**. Only use games and system files you have legally obtained. Games, keys and firmware are not included. ### Existing saves and settings Lichii uses its own profile: `%APPDATA%\lichii` on Windows, and the `lichii` directories under `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` on Linux and macOS. Without XDG overrides, these are `~/.local/share/lichii`, `~/.config/lichii` and `~/.cache/lichii`. An existing portable `user/` directory still takes priority and is not imported or changed by the wizard. On the first non-portable GUI launch, Lichii offers to import Eden and other detected emulator profiles. Back up `%APPDATA%\eden` first on Windows, or the old data, config and cache directories on Unix, and close the source emulator. Choose **Keep Old Data** to copy without changing the source, then check your saves and relaunch. Existing destination data is retained in backup directories rather than merged. Move also retains a source backup until you remove it yourself; Link deliberately shares settings and saves. Paths outside the imported data root remain shared and unchanged. An interrupted import offers recovery on the next launch. `eden-cli`, including `--help` and `--version`, refuses to initialize configuration until you import or explicitly choose **Start fresh** in the GUI. ## Compatibility and issue reports Compatibility and performance vary by game, hardware and driver. Rendering errors, stutters and crashes remain possible. Passing automated tests does not establish that a game renders correctly, and this project makes no universal frame-rate guarantee. Browse [community compatibility reports](https://lichii.zortos.me/reports) for results with each player's build and setup. Desktop reporting requires a build containing [PR #303](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/303) and is not available in build 88. In builds that include it, play and stop a Switch 2 game, then right-click that game and choose **Submit compatibility report**. Only the latest session in the current Lichii process is eligible. Confirm the matching website catalog entry and review the editable machine, game, setup, and enabled add-on details prefilled where available. Check the public preview and give explicit consent before submitting. Nothing uploads automatically, and the native v1 reporter does not read or upload logs or files. When [reporting an issue](https://github.com/zortos293/Eglantine/issues), include: - The exact build, game version, CPU, GPU and driver version. - Relevant settings and steps to reproduce the problem. - A screenshot and the log from the affected session, after checking it for personal information. Do not upload game files, keys, firmware or private account information. ## Building and contributing See the [build guide](docs/Build.md), [user documentation](docs/user/README.md) and [coding guidelines](docs/Coding.md). Some inherited documentation and internal build target names still use upstream names. The GUI build target is `lichii`; its output is `lichii.exe` on Windows and `lichii` on other desktop platforms. Star this repo!* Left: a TikTok ad shot on a phone. Right: an AI remake with another product. rea-video's verdict: the left is all live footage, one set and two camera positions; the right is all AI, 8 shots across 3 generations.
## Quick start rea-video is built for AI agents. In Claude Code, Codex or any agent that can run commands, say: ```text Install https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video, then break down this video: /path/to/video.mp4 ``` The agent installs the CLI, learns the workflow and runs the whole thing. You need ffmpeg and Python 3.10+. Breakdowns are fully upgraded. Each one gives you two outputs: - **Report** (`report.html` / PDF), for you: more reader-friendly, with a clearer structure, easier to learn from and to understand how the video was made and how to remake it. - **[VIDEO.md](https://videomd.github.io/videomd/)**, for your AI: layered, so the AI reads only what a question needs and uses fewer tokens. You can also hook up a video-capable model (Gemini or Doubao both work) by giving the agent its endpoint and key. That makes the live/AI/3D calls more accurate and adds a reverse-engineered prompt for every shot. It works fine without one; if your agent can see images, it checks the uncertain shots itself. > Reports are written in whichever language you ask in (Chinese or English). The example reports below are in English. ## What it can break down | Video type | Examples | What you get | |---|---|---| | Live footage | Talking-head, tabletop, handheld product demo, vlog, store visit | Setups and camera positions, framing, camera moves, lighting (12 setups with gear lists), color grade | | AI video | Text/image-to-video, AI short drama, AI music video | Evidence, a reverse-engineered prompt per shot, how to batch into generations and which model to use | | Avatar | A portrait driven by audio, lip-sync | Which shots are avatar shots, what portrait and audio you need | | 3D / animation | Blender / C4D explainers, product animation, 2D animation, stop-motion | Whether to generate with a video model or render from 3D code | | Code / template | Kinetic type, UI demos, charts, slide-style cards | Text, layout and motion timing, ready to rebuild as a Remotion project | | Screen recording | Software tutorials, web demos | Which parts are real material you'll need to record yourself | | Mixed / edits | AI characters + code UI + real screen capture; live footage with AI edits | Each shot judged separately, then reassembled on the original timeline | Besides how the visuals were made, every breakdown also covers: - Captions and styled text: start and end of each line (exports to SRT / ASS), plus color, outline and how the text comes in - Stickers, emoji, picture-in-picture: where they sit and how long they stay - Editing: where the cuts are, how fast, whether they hit the bea

# dsh-purge Community **让 AI 更专注地辅助你的学习与动手实验。** 给 DeepSeek Harness 的自托管控件（俗称「破甲」插件）· 86 条宿主补丁 · 25 层状态自检 · 左侧栏整页设置 [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kingcharleslzy-ai/dsh-purge?label=release)](https://github.com/kingcharleslzy-ai/dsh-purge/releases) [![Checks](https://github.com/kingcharleslzy-ai/dsh-purge/actions/workflows/community.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/kingcharleslzy-ai/dsh-purge/actions/workflows/community.yml) 当前版本 **1.7.14** · 适配 **DSH Desktop 0.2.2-rc.3**（0.2.2-rc.1 / 0.2.1-rc.1 / rc.2 / rc.3 / rc.5 同样通过） · [English](docs/README.en.md) 1.7.14 让侧栏与插件详情页共享同一份 Purge 设置，并同步维护页的更新偏好与错误状态。[发行说明](https://github.com/kingcharleslzy-ai/dsh-purge/releases/tag/v1.7.14)。 **原项目与作者**：小杨 / YuJunZhiXue 是历史上游 dsh-purge 的作者署名。本仓库独立维护社区版，保留上游版权和 MIT 许可证。历史署名不代表对当前同名 GitHub 账号身份的核实。详见[署名记录](NOTICE.md)与[许可证](LICENSE)。
--- ## 搭配插件 · [DSH-Spicy](https://github.com/kingcharleslzy-ai/DSH-Spicy) **完美适配 purge 的 nsfw content creation 插件** 用 Qwen Image 2.1 为成年虚构角色制作写真和插画，用参考图、LoRA 或蒙版调整造型。选定一张图后，用 MiniMax H3 拍成有声镜头，也可以让 Agent 按角色卡做分镜、逐镜审片，再剪成完整的成人向短片。图像和视频模型可部署在本机或自己的 GPU 服务器。 [打开 DSH-Spicy 的 GitHub 仓库](https://github.com/kingcharleslzy-ai/DSH-Spicy) ## 它是什么 dsh-purge Community 是一个跑在你自己机器上的 Harness 附加组件。它把日常使用里最消耗注意力的几件事收敛到一处： - **看清楚状态**：安装、补丁、注入到底有没有就绪，一条命令或一屏面板给结论； - **少一些往返**：把反复出现的确认与打断，收敛成一次设置； - **随时能回去**：应用、回滚、开关都留记录，操作前自动快照； - **方便做实验**：提示词、规则、预设集中管理，改坏了能撤。 目标很简单：**让助手更连贯地配合你的学习与动手实验**，而不是每做一步都先停下来问一句。 社区里通常把它叫作「破甲」或「无限制模式」插件——指的是它降低了交互层面的摩擦，让 agent 能连续执行任务；它不改模型本身，也不改变你要做的事。 ### 下载时报 `fetch failed`？ 1.6.39 起，独立安装器会显示失败阶段和错误码，有限重试后可切换系统 curl；两条通道都保留来源、证书和 SHA256 校验。请先重新下载安装脚本再运行 dry-run，仍失败时提交脱敏诊断行即可。见 [下载排查说明](docs/maintenance-issue-52.md)。不会自动修改代理或重启 DSH。 ### 让不同预设保留自己的提示词 1.6.40 新增 `excludePresets`：默认空列表，保持原有行为；可将 `roleplay`、`minimal` 等预设排除在 Purge 提示词注入之外，保留命令、面板与工具。切换预设、并行会话和子 Agent 各自判断，宿主兜底也遵守排除。配置示例、升级步骤与边界见 [按预设排除说明](docs/maintenance-issue-53.md)。这不会撤销全局宿主补丁。 ## 设计原则 | 原则 | 含义 | | --- | --- | | 本机优先 | 全部逻辑在本机运行，不改云端账号、不上传提示词或配置 | | 可见 | 每个动作都有状态与证据，不靠"应该生效了"这种判断 | | 可回滚 | 应用 / 安装 / 回滚前自动快照，保留原文件与校验清单 | | 不替你做决定 | 只减少摩擦，不改变你的目标；改什么、开什么，都由你确认 | ## 适用场景 本机学习、个人项目、自动化实验与维护工作。请在你拥有或已获授权的环境中使用；涉及他人系统时，先取得许可。 ## 1.6.39 更新 修复独立安装器只显示 `fetch failed` 的问题：分阶段诊断、有限重试和系统 curl 备用下载，继续严格校验官方来源、证书和 SHA256。下载失败不触碰现有安装。[发行说明](docs/releases/1.6.48.md) · [配置与验收](docs/maintenance-issue-52.md) ## 安装 手动选择 GitHub 源码文件夹时，先在含 `package-lock.json` 的插件根目录运行 `npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts`，再选择该目录。发行 TGZ 走下方官方安装流程。 **DSH 官方入口负责安装插件；下面的社区安装器由本仓库维护，不是 DeepSeek 官方脚本。** 首次安装可用官方界面或 CLI；已经装过 `dsh-purge` / 旧独立面板时，用社区安装器原地迁移，不要先卸载。安装、应用宿主补丁、手动重启是独立动作。 ### 方式一：DSH 官方界面（首次安装） 1. 先打开 DSH 完成初始化。按当前官方文档，进入「插件」，点击「实验性插件」旁的「更多」，启用「自定义插件市场」；然后进入「发现 → 添加索引源」。 2. 本项目的**社区索引**：`https://kingcharleslzy-ai.github.io/dsh-purge/index.json`。 3. 选择 dsh-purge Community，核对来源为 `kingcharleslzy-ai/dsh-purge`、包名为 `dsh-purge-community`，确认后安装。 界面和安装协议由 DSH 提供，索引与插件由社区维护。不同 DSH 版本的入口文字可能不同；第三方 `dsh-market` 也可能有额外的筛选与迁移限制。已有旧包时请使用方式三。[官方市场说明](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/guide/plugin-market.zh.md) ### 方式二：DSH 官方 CLI（首次安装） 下面命令适用于**已经安装 `dsh` 命令、且使用 `web` profile 的 CLI/Web 用户**，在 macOS/Linux 终端或 Windows PowerShell 中运行。桌面版用户优先用上面的界面；不要为了安装插件再用 `npx` 下载另一套宿主。 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add "https://github.com/kingcharleslzy-ai/dsh-purge/releases/download/v1.7.14/dsh-purge-community-1.7.14.tgz" ``` `web` 必须与实际启动的 profile 一致；自定义数据目录需要沿用该实例的 `DSH_HOME`。命令使用本次发行的固定版本 URL；不是 `npm install -g`，也不是安装裸 npm 包名。本项目通过 GitHub 发行，**不要替换成 `add dsh-purge` 或 `add dsh-purge-community`**。官方 CLI 的安装不会额外运行我们安装器的 Release SHA256 比对及迁移快照；需要这些功能时选方式三。[官方 CLI 安装说明](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.zh.md) ### 方式三：社区安装器（备份、旧版迁移、恢复） 先安装并打开一次 DSH，让实际 profile 初始化。以下命令下载**本仓库的脚本**，先校验，再安装；`dry-run` 通过仅代表前置检查、下载和 SHA256 通过，不代表依赖安装、迁移或启动已通过。请先阅读下载的脚本。 #### macOS Desktop 默认应用位置 `/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app`、数据目录 `~/.dsh`、profile `desktop`。将下面两段放在同一个终端会话中执行： ```sh PURGE_INSTALL_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" curl -fSL --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 90 "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kingcharleslzy-ai/dsh-purge/master/scripts/install.sh" -o "$PURGE_INSTALL_DIR/install.sh" sh "$PURGE_INSTALL_DIR/install.sh" --dry-run ``` 校验成功、核对目标实例后执行： ```sh sh "$PURGE_INSTALL_DIR/install.sh" ``` 自定义应用或 home 时，先设置 `DSH_APP` / `DSH_HOME`；自定义 profile 对两次命令都加 `--profile=实际名称`。不要照抄别人的路径。 profile 为 `desktop`，带独立 dsh CLI 的新壳默认为 `web`；自定义 profile 用 `-Profile` 指定。不要求管理员权限；路径含空格也支持。 ```powershell $PurgeInstaller = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('purge-install-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N') + # 中小学·高中知识图谱（数学 + 语文 + 科学 + 英语 + 物理 + 历史 + 地理 + 生物 + 化学）

对齐《义务教育数学课程标准（2022 年版 2025 年修订）》（教育部《中小学课程方案和课程标准日常修订版》，教材〔2025〕1 号）、《普通高中数学课程标准（2017年版2025年修订）》的**必修和选择性必修**，以及《义务教育英语课程标准（2022年版）》一级、二级和三级（7–9 年级）和《普通高中英语课程标准（2017年版2025年修订）》的必修、选择性必修。数学教材是人教版一–九、人教 A 版（2019）必修两册和选择性必修三册；英语按人教 PEP（三年级起点，根据2022年版课程标准修订的新版）三上到六上（四下按 2026 春 pep4x_2026 densify；五下新版未上线暂按现行 peps5x densify；六下按现行 peps6x densify）、人教版 Go for it! 新版七上到九上（九下新版未上线，暂按旧版九年级全一册第 9–14 单元等），以及人教版（2019）高中必修三册和选择性必修四册。初中物理按人教版新版（根据2022年版课程标准修订）八年级上册、八年级下册、九年级全一册，对齐《义务教育物理课程标准（2022年版2025年修订）》；高中物理按人教版（2019年审定）必修第一至三册和选择性必修第一至三册，对齐《普通高中物理课程标准（2017年版2020年修订）》。附**自适应前置诊断**与题库。数学答错会沿先修边从高中、初中一直回溯到具体的小学知识点。英语单独成图，不和数学连边；初中英语会连回小学英语，高中英语主要连回初中英语。物理也单独成图，用到的数学写在知识点的 `mathLinks` 字段里，不算先修边。仓库名仍是 `cn-math-taxonomy`。初中生物按人教版七至八年级单独成图，对齐《义务教育生物学课程标准（2022年版）》第四学段内容要求的公开转述；六三制九年级没有生物课。初中化学按人教版九年级上、下册单独成图，对齐《义务教育化学课程标准（2022年版）》第四学段内容要求的公开转述；六三制化学在九年级开设，不建七、八年级化学点，也不采用五四制全一册。高中化学必修第一册、必修第二册、选择性必修第一册《化学反应原理》、选择性必修第二册《物质结构与性质》和选择性必修第三册《有机化学基础》按人教版印刷目录成图，对齐《普通高中化学课程标准（2017年版）》相关内容要求的公开转述。初中语文按统编版七至九年级并入已有语文学科（仍是 `subject=chinese`，编号 `cnc_j`），对齐《义务教育语文课程标准（2022年版）》第四学段学段要求的公开转述（2026-11-06 对照人教社电子书印刷页 14–16；该节没有【内容要求】标题，也未取得教育部 PDF）；小学语文仍是 `cnc_p`。没有高中语文。

**范围：数学高中做到必修和选择性必修，并且只用人民教育出版社 A 版（2019）；英语做到三年级到高中（人教版 2019 必修三册、选择性必修四册）；语文做到小学一至六年级和初中七至九年级（统编版），没有高中语文。** 7.3「复数的三角表示」仍按教材选学处理，没有单独建点。定积分不在选择性必修的内容要求里，没有建点。英语不出听力和口语题。

# ub-mode

`ub-mode` is an agent skill that enforces disciplined software engineering principles when writing or changing code. It is loosely based on portions of [@poteto](https://github.com/poteto)'s rules (`poteto-mode` / `pstack`), reduced and paired with deterministic quality-gate tools:

1. **First Make it Work** — Laziness Protocol, Foundational Thinking, TDD, Redesign From First Principles, Attack the Premise, Subtract Before You Add, Outcome-Oriented Execution, Build the Lever, and Architecture (Model the Domain, Boundary Discipline, Type System Discipline, Make Operations Idempotent, Separate Before Serializing Shared State).
2. **Then Make it Right** — Fix Root Causes, Sequence Work into Verifiable Units, Test Behavior (Not Implementation), [Crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper) (`CRAP < 10`), [Dryer](https://github.com/unclebob/dryer) (duplication `< 0.8`), [Mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) (cover the uncovered, kill the survivors, delete dead code), and Refactoring.
3. **Practice** — Keep a Log, Guard the Context Window, Worktree Cleanup, and Commit and Push in small ordered commits.

## Companion Tool Repositories

`ub-mode` relies on deterministic quality-gate tools to enforce structure, complexity, duplication, and test thoroughness:

- [unclebob/crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper) — Computes cyclomatic complexity, test coverage, and CRAP score per function so every function stays under the CRAP threshold (`< 10`).
- [unclebob/dryer](https://github.com/unclebob/dryer) — Detects structural code duplication so duplicate blocks (`>= 0.8` similarity) are eliminated.
- [unclebob/mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) — Runs mutation testing to expose uncovered code and surviving mutants that tests fail to catch.
- [unclebob/uml-viewer](https://github.com/unclebob/uml-viewer) — Visualizes components, coverage, CRAP, mutation scores, and dependency directions.

## Installation

Copy `SKILL.md` into your agent's skills directory as `ub-mode/SKILL.md` (for example `~/.grok/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`, `~/.claude/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`, or `~/.cursor/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`), then invoke `/ub-mode`.
